description: FTLR-0 / SCIP-PILOT formal anchor registry (issue #299), extended by FDG-0 Phase B formal facets (issue #298). This file is the SOLE cross-domain authority binding C++ semantic authorities to formal claims. C++-internal relationships are never recorded here; they are recovered mechanically from the SCIP index (scip-clang over the selected Xmake build world). Suite ids must match spec/tla/manifest.json. Claim ids follow the S1A property matrix (docs/investigations/s1a-formal-coverage.md); F02/F05/F07/F09/F10 are intentionally not seeded in this pilot (bounded corpus). Schema 2 adds OPTIONAL per-anchor ids and OPTIONAL per-claim facets: facets are internal subdivisions of an existing claim (never new claims); every facet suite must belong to the parent claim and the facet-suite union must equal the parent set (overlap allowed, loss/expansion forbidden); facet routing is anchor/path-derived and a facet NEVER creates a narrower answer where trust is missing (facet precision optional, claim-level conservatism required). Facet mapping provenance is EXPLICIT (hand-maintained cross-domain authority). This registry is experiment-scoped: it is a precursor schema for the #298 FDG-0 correspondence registry, not a replacement for any existing authority.

claims.title: terminal winner / exactly-once

cpp_anchors.note: first backend_ready terminal wins under the leaf mutex; losers never overwrite
blocking backend producer of real terminals

io_uring backend producer of real terminals. The default xmake config compiles this TU in UNSUPPORTED-STUB mode (the terminal machinery is compiled out), so this anchor resolves only in an index built with `xmake f --with-liburing=y`. A default-config check reports it as a config-gated unresolved anchor: a visible declared gap, not a silent miss.

claims.notes: Contract: exactly one terminal per accepted generation; Scheme-B single-domain arbitration. Model coverage spans request-arena (NEG-RA-1), e10-waitnode (primitive domain), e13 select winner linearization.
